summary: I settled the five merge conflicts, keeping both sides, and built SL-089's seam proofs on top. The pieces: the hook's rows dump (a passive `rows` mode, with the unreadable-folders tab selected on EndingShown), window cases N-005 (SMB), N-006 (cloud, three endings), T-009 (held folder), W-001 (panel against the engine's record, with an open oracle and its own controls), R-002 panel-row reveal steps (f) and (g), and the Core.Tests twins. This attempt fixes only what the engine stopped. N-006 ran its four rig runs one after another and needed about 7 minutes, and its timeout control alone took 121 s. It now runs them side by side on roots of their own and ends the timeout control at the filter's first timeout (60.4 s). The whole case takes 70 s and passes, its sync roots are unregistered and deleted, and the O-023 and O-024 mutations each make it fail. No product code changed; uat's merge already carries core.unreadable, which the new twinned rule guards.

files.why: Merge conflict settled: uat's SL-095 settled rules kept, then SL-089's settled comment. It also carries the twinned TheWindowReportReadsOnlyTheFailedFolderCount entry (single-line pattern, (?m), including_comments). Rule 2 is dropped.
Merge conflict settled: uat's S14-S38 and SL-089's F36-F40/P28-P31 rows both kept. The note's row count is corrected to 89 (uat's said 68 while holding 80).
Merge conflict settled by taking uat's side, which already writes core.unreadable. The result is identical to uat.
Merge settled (uat's settings mode plus SL-089's rows mode). Adds the passive rows mode, FSA_HOOK_ROWS for rows and stop, and the Stop stamp.
The panel's rows dump: selects the tab on EndingShown, reads items and drawn texts, writes JSONL at ShutdownStarted. SL-095's NotScannedRow items are kept apart from the rows.

Merge settled. Adds N-005, N-006, T-009, W-001 and R-002 steps f and g. This attempt splits N-006's run into Start-CloudSeamRun, Step-CloudSeamRun and Complete-CloudSeamRun, so its four runs go side by side and the timeout control ends at the filter's first timeout: the case now takes 70 s.
O-029's corpus: 15 row shapes, bounded by who produces them, with the class expected and what the pre-m3 oracle gave.
Runs WindowCases.ps1's own oracle, checker controls and verdict functions against real planted folders.
ParseScript, Load and Pwsh made internal so W001OracleTests reuses them.
Default-suite twin of T-009 (h recorded 32; c and p not recorded; LastAccessAsked-Kept>=2).
Feeds the twinned rule's pattern the shapes it must catch and the look-alikes it must leave.
A folder held without read sharing, and the scanner's two folder opens.
Deny at open, a trace of creates and the hold, and SweepLeftBehind for killed runs (review M5).
The stop-seam scenario (held fetches, failure completion via CfExecute) and unregister/probe/delete teardown with a reparse-point fallback (review M6).
The measured results (now including the 60.4 s timeout ending and the 70 s side-by-side run), the Q-177 platform-limit and silent-undercount record, and the owner's whole-C:\ W-001 command.

obligations.how: N-005 serves s held by the SMB rig and kills the rig 8 s after the logged hold. The control (no Stop) put s in as NothingListed 59. With Stop, s has no row. Passed on this PC.

N-005 uses the rig's create log for t and u: the server never opened them after Stop. The control lit both (53), and the main run has no row for either. On the cloud rig, N-006 measured that no ending lights t or u, so their absence is reported as the Q-177 platform limit.

In N-005 and N-006, a (refused at open) and b (failpoint b|3|59) are rows once each. Header N = core.unreadable = dump rows = 2. The case checks that a's refused create, b's failpoint and s's hold were all logged before the Stop, and is inconclusive otherwise; all three held.

N-006 holds s's fetch, presses Stop 2 s later, and releases it 8 s after the hold through CfExecute with a failure status. There is no row for s. No control ending lit s, so the result is reported under the Q-177 platform-limit verdict. Passes in 70 s.

T-009 holds h without read sharing first, then adds the deny on write-attributes, and probes 5/32 before the scan. Its row is NothingListed 32, drawn 'could not be opened: in use by another program', and 'access denied' appears nowhere. The Core Fact checks the same thing in the default suite.
In T-009, c refuses the keep-last-access open but is held by nobody (5/0). It is not a row, and core.unreadable is 1.
In N-005, b's 1,200 46-character names fill page 3 and the failpoint fired on b page 3 over SMB. The row is ListedPartway 59, drawn 'only partly read: network or share error'.
W-001 on C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER: 446 rows, 7 drawn. Header 446 = core.unreadable 446 = dump rows. No duplicate, no empty reason; both hook and checker ran unelevated.

W-001's oracle opens every code-5 NothingListed row with the scanner's plain mask and lists nothing. On C:\Windows\Logs (12 refused-then-listed folders at its top level) it found 1 row, still refused, and 0 leaks.
Corpus rows F11 (363 → leftover-363), F13 (code 5 on a junction → leftover-reparse) and F12 (1920 → other-code) run against real folders in W001OracleTests.
Corpus row F08 (code 2, recreated after the scan start → other-code, never opened) and F04 (code 5 recreated → changed-since-scan) run in W001OracleTests.
R-002 step (f) reveals the 300-character deny-all folder from its panel row: Exact, hr 0, landed at 1167 ms. Parent and single selection checked by Name; no dialog, no consent.exe.
R-002 step (g) uses a 1000-character list-denied, non-hidden folder. Revealed from its panel row: Exact, hr 0, landed at 913 ms, with the same Name-only checks.
Added the passive hook mode 'rows': it presses nothing, has no deadline, and arms the failpoint. T-009, W-001 and every control run use it.
The dump, the assertions and the record use NothingListed. W-001 asserts nothingListed + listedPartway = rows, and opened + tallied = nothingListed.
Rule 2 is gone from fitness.yaml; only rule 1 is twinned. rules-parity reports AGREE 16 facts, 20 twinned, 40 patterns.

mutation.replace:
- name: 'TheShippedAppNeverDumpsPanelRows (*.cs)'
    files: 'src/**'
    must_not_import:
      - 'FsaWindowHook*'
    must_not_match:
      - '(?m)FSA_HOOK_ROWS'
    including_comments: true
    because: 'the shipped app never dumps panel rows, as the design declared it'

  - name: 'TheWindowReportReadsOnlyTheFailedFolderCount (*.cs)'

obligations.how: The pattern holds on one line, with its own Fact and twin. Plant F36 (two-line fluent layout) to F40 must fire and P28-P31 must stay quiet. WindowReportRuleTests feeds the shapes to the Fact's pattern.

Each N-005 run kills the rig, waits for the app, then sweeps exactly the rig's own mappings under RigLock. After each run the case asserts no 127.0.0.1 mapping is left. Rig start retries on error 53 for up to 75 s. A final sweep runs in the case's finally.

mutation.find: Remove-RigMappingsLeft # the kill's own leftover, before anything looks (review M5)
mutation.replace: # the kill's leftover is not swept (review M5 undone)

obligations.how: Every N-006 run ends in Complete-CloudSeamRun: stop the provider, undo the deny, unregister, probe, then delete with the reparse-point fallback. The case asserts NOT-REGISTERED and the folder gone. Roots live under LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\fsa-window-cloud while TEMP is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. Clear-StaleCloudRoots cleans up independently at start and end. The runs now go side by side, so `-Case N-006 -IncludeCloud` passes in 70 s with all 4 roots removed and the base folder gone. The mutation below made it fail in about 70 s, and teardown still left nothing.

N-006 runs three controls (release, kill, timeout) beside the main run. The timeout control ends on the filter's own timeout of the held fetch (60.4 s), after which every later fetch is failed. Each control asserts the scan ends, prints core files/folders/bytes, and for kill and timeout fails on any row for s. No ending lit s, so the main run reports 'held: platform gives no failed read (Q-177)'. The record is in docs/design/SL-089-seams.md. The case passes in 70 s; the mutation below gave exit 3 (inconclusive).

W-001 never scans C:\ unattended: -Root is mandatory, and here it ran on two bounded roots (pool +2 MB). It records kernel pool before and after, and on a whole drive requires the wcifs-layer-store precaution on. The C:\ run is the owner's.
obligations.not_mutable: The fix is where W-001 runs and by whom. No test can observe that from the inside, and the whole-drive precaution check only fires on a whole-drive root, which this build may not scan.

obligations.how: Get-CheckerControls opens C:\Windows, gets 5 on a planted deny-ListDirectory folder, and opens a planted refused-then-listed folder. Get-W001Verdict returns inconclusive unless all three held, and the record carries checkerControls.
Rule 2 is deleted from fitness.yaml. The SL-089 settled comment cites SL-033's 'the shipped app carries no test seam'.
obligations.not_mutable: Re-adding a settled duplicate of an existing settled rule changes nothing a test observes. The twinned form is O-020's mutation.

obligations.how: RowsMode selects UnreadableTab inside EndingShown, reads the realised containers then, keeps them, and writes at ShutdownStarted. T-009 requires drawn text.

mutation.find: tab.IsSelected = true; // what a click on its header sets
mutation.replace: // tab left as the ending chose

obligations.how: The oracle opens only code-5 NothingListed rows. It tallies 363, reparse-point rows and other codes, exempts rows whose CreationTime or ChangeTime is after the scan start, and tallies folders gone since. The pre-m3 oracle failed F03, F04, F06, F07, F09 and F10 as leaks; the current one passes all 15.

HeldFolderReasonTests probes both opens per folder before the scan. It asserts LastAccessAsked - LastAccessKept >= 2, and that c and p are listed with their files. The mutation was run once here and the Fact failed.

mutation.find: kept = TryOpenKeepingLastAccess(boxOff, win32Path, access, flags, out opened);
mutation.replace: { kept = TryOpenKeepingLastAccess(boxOff, win32Path, access, flags, out opened); if (!kept) error = 5; }

obligations.how: b's children are pinned at 1,200 names of 46 characters, so page 3 is a full data page. Every control and main run asserts 'fail-listing fired b page 3'; it fired in every run.

mandatory.where: WindowCases.ps1 Test-N005 (SMB: control lights s, t, u; with Stop, only a and b once each) and Test-N006 (cloud: three endings plus main side by side in 70 s; only a and b, no s/t/u row, the Q-177 platform limit). Rows are read through the hook's rows dump (RowsMode.cs); core.unreadable in the schema-1 report must agree.
Test-T009 and HeldFolderReasonTests (held folder: 'in use by another program', 32). N-005's b row: 'only partly read: network or share error', 59, over the SMB rig.

Test-W001: rows = header = core.unreadable, no duplicate, no empty reason, oracle with controls, counts-only record. Run here on WER (446 rows) and Windows\Logs. The whole-C:\ recorded run is the owner's (review M8 disposition): `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 -Root C:\`.
Test-R002 steps (f) and (g) with Check-PanelLanding: 300 and 1000 characters from panel rows, landed in 1167 and 913 ms, Name-only checks, hr 0, no dialog or consent.exe.

N-005, N-006 and R-002 were run here unattended, each asserting its own cleanup: no 127.0.0.1 mapping; sync roots unregistered and their folders gone; own Explorer windows closed. Default filters are untouched. W-001 was not run over C:\ (review M8).

Test-N006 runs release, kill and timeout controls (the timeout one at the filter's first timeout, 60.4 s). Each asserts the scan ends with no s row and prints totals. The main run reports 'held: platform gives no failed read (Q-177)'. docs/design/SL-089-seams.md records the platform limit and the silent undercount.

deviations: The design's T-008 is built as T-009: T-008 already exists (SL-082's refused-failpoint case).
The design's 'core.unreadable' component needed no code: uat's SL-095 merge already writes it, so WindowReport.cs is identical to uat. SL-089's twinned rule guards that line.
The rows dump handles SL-095's NotScannedRow items, which share UnreadableList with failed rows. They are written as separate 'notScanned' lines and never counted.
Q-177's platform-limit verdict is applied to t and u on the cloud rig as well as s. O-002 measured that the provider failing their fetches never made them rows under any ending.

N-005 runs its control and main run in one -Case invocation, and N-006 runs its three controls and main run in one invocation, so the main verdict can read its controls. -Control runs the controls alone.

N-006's four runs go side by side on separate sync roots, and the timeout control ends at the filter's first timeout of the held fetch (60.4 s). The design ran them one after another, and the timeout control waited out the second timeout (121 s). That cannot fit the 120 s the engine gives a test command; the held fetch has already ended by the filter's timeout by then, and later fetches are failed as under release, which the release control already covers. The earlier sequential runs, which waited the full 121 s, gave the same result (no row).
W-001's -Root is mandatory and was run here on two bounded roots. The whole-C:\ run is the owner's (review M8 disposition).
W-001 writes .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json only for a whole C: drive. Other roots go to artifacts/w001-run.json (gitignored).
The plants.json note's row count is corrected to 89. uat's note said 68 while its rows were already 80.
not_built: The whole-C:\ W-001 recorded run (c-drive-run.json): left to the owner, because of the pool cost (review M8).
A rules-harness run recording plants F36-F40 and P28-P31: it needs the engine's interpreter (Q-027 assigns it to validate).
m6 and m7 were waived to SC-133 and SC-134 and are not built here.
follow_ups: Owner runs `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case W-001 -Root C:\` unelevated for criterion 3.
Validate runs the rules harness for F36-F40 and P28-P31 (Q-027) and records the outcomes in plants.json.
Cloud placeholder folders whose provider fails or never answers are listed as empty with no mark: a silent undercount (Q-177), and a candidate slice.
The three LastAccess/HeldOpenTree failures (Q-190) still keep the full suite red (556/559).

Failed as they must. O-023's mutation gave exit 1 (folder left); O-024's gave exit 3 (inconclusive). About 70 s each; file restored byte-exact, no root left.
